questions.worked_solution:
The sum takes integer values of $n$ from $1$ to $4.$ So, computing the terms for $n=1,2,3,4$ and then adding them, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}\frac{3n+2}{6} & =(\frac{3(1)+2}{6})+(\frac{3(2)+2}{6})+(\frac{3(3)+2}{6})+(\frac{3(4)+2}{6}) \\  & =(\frac{3+2}{6})+(\frac{6+2}{6})+(\frac{9+2}{6})+(\frac{12+2}{6}) \\  & =\frac{5}{6}+\frac{8}{6}+\frac{11}{6}+\frac{14}{6} \\  & =\frac{5+8+11+14}{6} \\  & =\frac{38}{6} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{2}\cdot 19}{\cancel{2}\cdot 3} \\  & =\frac{19}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Notice that the terms of the corresponding sequence

$$
5,\,10,\,15,\,…,\,145,\,150.
$$

 are multiples of $5,$ and since $150÷5=30,$ there are $30$ terms in total. 

Therefore, the $n$th term of the sequence has the form

$$
{a}_{n}=5n,
$$

where $n$ ranges from $n=1$ to $n=30.$ Indeed: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =5(1)=5 \\ {a}_{2} & =5(2)=10 \\ {a}_{3} & =5(3)=15 \\  & \,\,⋮ \\ {a}_{29} & =5(29)=145 \\ {a}_{30} & =5(30)=150\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}S=5+10+15+⋯+145+150={\sum }_{n=1}^{30}5n.\end{aligned}
$$

The sum takes integer values of $a$ from $1$ to $3.$ So, computing the terms for $a=1,2,3$ and then adding them, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{a=1}^{3}a{(\frac{1}{2})}^{a+1} & =1{(\frac{1}{2})}^{1+1}+2{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2+1}+3{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3+1} \\  & =1{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+2{(\frac{1}{2})}^{3}+3{(\frac{1}{2})}^{4} \\  & =1\cdot \frac{1}{4}+2\cdot \frac{1}{8}+3\cdot \frac{1}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{8}+\frac{3}{16} \\  & =\frac{(1\cdot 4)+(2\cdot 2)+3}{16} \\  & =\frac{4+4+3}{16} \\  & =\frac{11}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
